long_biography.plain_text:
A stalled Washington property market gave Joey Kaempfer the opening for his defining second act. Former employer Alan Glen proposed taking the outlet-mall model to Europe. Kaempfer accepted, secured British Airports Authority as a capital partner and opened the first McArthurGlen centre within 16 months. The wager helped establish designer outlets as a mainstream European retail format.

Kaempfer had learned development through Levitt, Alan Glen and Wallace Holladay before founding his own Washington firm on his 30th birthday. That company grew from town houses into architecturally ambitious offices, survived a severe early-1990s property collapse and was eventually acquired by Vornado. McArthurGlen became his enduring platform: founder-led and later partnered with Simon Property Group, it combines outlet retail with his longstanding emphasis on architecture, public space and destination design.
